fingerprints.story: The sea was a sheet of hammered pewter under a sky the colour of old bone. For forty years, Elias had watched it from the lantern room of the St. Jude’s Point lighthouse, a solitary sentinel against the grey. His world was one of polished brass, the steady sweep of the light, and the rhythmic groan of the tide against the granite base. It was a life measured in the turning of gears and the slow, inexorable march of time.
